primary_meaning: Sudden, total, and irreversible destruction or judgment (something cast down never to rise again)

alternatives.meaning: Power of faith to remove or overcome seemingly immovable obstacles
Severe divine punishment preferred over causing 'little ones' (believers) to stumble
Chaotic removal, burial, or obliteration into the abyss/depths (general apocalyptic imagery of downfall)

notes: The image appears in multiple distinct NT and OT contexts; the irreversible-judgment reading (especially millstone/Babylon) is the most frequently cited in Christian teaching and commentaries, but the faith-mountain saying and the offense-millstone warning are equally well-known and not reducible to a single unified symbol. No single settled meaning covers every occurrence of stone/mountain/tree/ship/millstone cast into the sea.
